one_liner: Freshworks cloud helpdesk for ticketing and customer support.

evidence.claim: REST API with JSON over HTTP and standard verbs; v2 docs list dozens of endpoints (tickets, ticket fields, forms, conversations, etc.)
evidence.quote: Freshdesk's APIs belong to the Representational State Transfer (REST) category.

evidence.claim: Authentication via personal API key used as basic-auth username with dummy password
evidence.quote: You can use your personal API key to authenticate the request. If you use the API key, there is no need for a password. You can use any set of characters as a dummy password.

evidence.claim: API key is self-serve from the agent's Profile Settings
evidence.quote: On the right pane, you will find the API Key

evidence.claim: Legacy free Sprout plan has no API access; current plans list includes Free, Growth, Pro, Enterprise with the article applying to them
evidence.quote: Note: If your account is on the Sprout plan, the API key and the API functionality will NOT be available.

evidence.claim: Official Freshworks MCP server for Freshdesk exists (EAP), authenticating with API key only
evidence.quote: The Freshworks Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI tools like Cursor and Claude to securely connect and interact with Freshdesk.

notes: Basic auth requires Base64-encoding 'APIKEY:X'. No OAuth 2.0 for product APIs per Freshworks community staff ('Currently, no Product API from Freshworks offers OAuth 2.0-based API consumption.'). Official MCP server is in EAP and API-key-only, exposing ticket/conversation tools (createTicket, fetchTickets, replyTicket, etc.). Rate limits can be raised by purchasing additional API calls. Sprout (legacy free plan) lacks API access; whether the current Free plan includes API keys is not explicitly stated, though the support article's plan applicability suggests only Sprout is excluded. Some admin endpoints (e.g., /api/v2/admin/ticket_fields) require admin-role API keys. No native GraphQL endpoint.
